notes.meaning: A massive crowd in heaven bursts into joyful singing. They praise God with 'Hallelujah,' an ancient Hebrew phrase meaning 'praise the Lord.' They celebrate because full deliverance, honor, and sovereign power belong only to Him.

God is praised because His decisions and punishments are entirely fair and true. He has judged the corrupt world system that dragged people into sin and false worship. By this judgment, God answers the cries of His people and avenges the blood of His faithful servants.

The voices in heaven call out their praise a second time with another joyful shout. The rising smoke proves that the corrupt city has been destroyed once and for all. God's people can celebrate knowing that this evil power will never return to harm anyone.

The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fall on their faces before God's throne in deep worship. Representing both God's redeemed people and all of His creation, they gladly agree with His judgment. They cry out 'Amen, Hallelujah,' confirming that God's actions are good and worthy of praise.

A voice speaks from near the throne, inviting all of God's servants to join the song. It calls on everyone who reveres the Lord, whether they are considered lowly or important in human eyes. No follower of God is left out of this call to praise Him.

John hears a mighty sound rolling like crashing ocean waves and roaring thunder. A vast crowd declares that the Lord God Almighty is actively taking up His royal rule over all creation. With the downfall of worldly oppressors, His eternal kingdom stands out clearly for all to see.

The heavenly hosts urge one another to rejoice because the wedding day of Christ, the Lamb, has finally arrived. His bride, the Church, has prepared herself for this long-awaited day. This wedding shows the loving and everlasting bond between Christ and His redeemed people.

The bride receives bright, clean linen to wear as a gracious gift from her Lord. This clean garment stands for the righteous deeds and pure living of God's holy people. Her simple, spotless beauty stands in sharp contrast to the gaudy, corrupt clothing of the worldly empire.

differ.view: Some Baptists see the fine linen as Christ's own righteousness credited to believers by faith, rather than good works done by believers.
Methodists understand the fine linen as the personal holiness and righteous acts produced in believers' lives by the Holy Spirit.

notes.meaning: An angel tells John to write a special blessing for everyone invited to the Lamb's wedding feast. Being invited means sharing in the eternal joy and comfort that the gospel promises. The angel guarantees that these encouraging words are completely dependable because they come from God Himself.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching sees the earthly celebration of the Eucharist, or Holy Communion, as a foretaste of this heavenly wedding banquet.

notes.meaning: Overcome with awe, John falls down before the angel, but the angel immediately stops him. The messenger explains that he is only a fellow servant alongside John and every believer who shares the message about Jesus. Worship belongs only to God, and the true purpose of prophecy is to point people to Jesus.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics view John's bow not as an attempt to offer divine worship, but as deep respect shown to an angel, which differs from the adoration owed to God alone.

notes.meaning: Heaven opens wide, revealing Jesus riding on a white horse as a victorious warrior King. He is called Faithful and True because He keeps every promise and carries out God's decrees without fail. When He judges and goes to war, He does so with perfect righteousness rather than selfish ambition.

His eyes burn like fiery flames, showing that He sees all things clearly and judges with complete wisdom. He wears many royal crowns on His head, proving His absolute authority over every nation and power. He also bears a written name that only He can fully comprehend, pointing to the limitless depths of His divine nature.

The divine warrior wears a robe dipped in blood, picturing the defeat of His enemies and the price of redemption. He is called 'The Word of God,' showing that He is God's ultimate message and truth made visible. Through Him, God speaks, creates, and carries out His final purposes.

The armies of heaven follow right behind the King, riding on white horses and dressed in clean, bright linen. This host includes the holy angels and God's redeemed people. They share in the King's triumphant procession without needing to fight the battle themselves.

A sharp sword comes out of the King's mouth, showing that His spoken word carries the power to strike down rebellious nations. He will rule all defiant powers with an unbreakable iron rod, shattering their resistance completely. He stomps out the winepress, carrying out the full and fiery anger of Almighty God against sin.

A majestic title is clearly written on His robe and across His thigh for everyone to see: King of kings and Lord of lords. This title declares that He holds the highest authority over every earthly monarch and ruler. No power in heaven or on earth can ever challenge His rightful reign.

An angel stands in the bright light of the sun and calls out to all scavenger birds in the sky. He invites them to a grim feast called the great banquet of God, which stands in stark contrast to the Lamb's joyful wedding supper. This picture shows the complete downfall of all who rebel against God, proving that rulers, soldiers, and ordinary people fall equally before His judgment.

The beast and the rulers of the earth assemble their vast armies to wage war against the King on the horse and His followers. Even when facing the Lord of heaven, rebellious human powers foolishly attempt to resist Him. Yet all their gathered might is utterly helpless before God's power.

The beast and the false prophet, who deceived people through false miracles into taking the beast's mark, are quickly captured. Without any long struggle, these two deceitful leaders are hurled alive into the burning lake of sulfur. This decisive act brings a permanent end to their lies and tyranny.

The remaining hostile soldiers are slain by the sword that comes from the mouth of the King, meaning they fall under the authority of His spoken word. The birds of the sky feast on their bodies, fulfilling the grim summons given earlier. God's truth thoroughly overcomes every enemy, leaving His people safe under His rule.
